messages.author: 4a5459c655bd0648
messages.subject: Zero inflated indicators
parts: I am using SEM and my measurement model includes around 15 items that are all rated on a 0-10 scale but highly skewed towards zero. I am wondering whether there is a way to estimate the measurement model with poisson corrections for zero inflation in R? Or would you assume that it should be sufficient to just run a generalised structural equation model that relaxes the normality assumption? Thank you!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Zero inflated indicators
parts: I am wondering whether there is a way to estimate the measurement model with poisson corrections for zero inflation in R?
lavaan does not yet have the capability to model zero inflated outcomes.
Or would you assume that it should be sufficient to just run a generalised structural equation model that relaxes the normality assumption?

I don't know, but I would imagine it depends on the proportion of zeros, sample size (needs to be large enough to estimate 10 thresholds per item), and model size.  You can post general question like this on the much larger forum SEMNET:

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html
